fun_why: Three seconds of a still view with one clap: nothing to see or replay, and the 'answer' from the island is a reverb tail of about 0.3 s that is hard to tell apart from a dry sample.
real_change: nightclap.jl (identical in live/ and plugins/) adds a NightClap system. At night, every 45 s, it casts 1500 random rays from Lumi's head and marches them against the terrain heightfield only: the first ground hit plus one mirror bounce. It keeps the arrival time of each hit and draws up to 400 small emissive spheres that light up at 60x slowed sound speed, so a ring spreads over the grass. That is a visualisation: nothing moves, collides or reacts to it, and it skips trees and props (left for todo #622). It also returns early when path tracing is on, so it can never appear in a traced film like this one. The audio comes from physics/echo.jl, which is from session 129 and unchanged here. That file does real BVH acoustic ray tracing with a convolved synthetic clap, so the sound is simulated. The picture is only a fixed camera.
real_why: The sound behind the film is real geometric acoustics (BVH rays, the listener's line of sight, travel time at 343 m/s). This session's code adds only a terrain-only ray march that drives glowing dots, a picture of the sound rather than more simulation.
summary: A 3.5 s static daytime shot of yellow planks, cattails and a tree, with a single clap at about 0.5 s and then 2.8 s of silence. Nobody is seen clapping, nothing in the picture answers the sound, and the session's own plugin (a night-time glow ring) is not in the film at all.
surprise_why: The acoustic tracer was already shown last session. Here it comes out as one short dry clap over a still shot of planks, and the new glow ring, which would have been the twist, never appears.
